prompts.title: Sample: Weekly Team Update
prompts.description: Turns raw weekly notes into a short, upbeat team update.
prompts.full_prompt:
Act as an experienced team lead who writes clear, upbeat updates.

Context:
I lead a small team and send a weekly update every Friday.

Task:
Turn my notes into a weekly update that covers wins, blockers and next week's priorities.

Input:
My notes: [MEETING NOTES]

Output format:
Three short sections (Wins, Blockers, Next week) with up to three bullets each.

Constraints:
- Under 150 words.
- Friendly, professional tone.
- Use only the facts in my notes.

Quality criteria:
- A colleague can read it in under a minute.
- Nothing is invented.
prompts.expected_output: A 120-word update with three short sections.

example_inputs.MEETING NOTES: Shipped the invoice export; waiting on vendor API keys; plan to start testing Monday.

prompts.example_output: Wins: invoice export shipped. Blockers: vendor API keys. Next week: start testing.
prompts.why_it_works: A fixed structure and a facts-only rule keep the update short and trustworthy.
customization_tips: Add your team's name and tone.

prompts.title: Sample: Meeting Decision Summary
prompts.description: Extracts only the decisions and owners from meeting notes.
prompts.full_prompt:
Act as a careful project coordinator.

Context:
We held a meeting and I need a record of what was decided.

Task:
List every decision with its owner and date.

Input:
[MEETING NOTES]

Output format:
A table with columns Decision, Owner, Date.

Constraints:
- Write 'Not stated' when the owner or date is missing.

Quality criteria:
- Only decisions that were actually agreed appear in the table.
prompts.why_it_works: The 'Not stated' rule prevents invented owners and dates.
